title: Too Close to Speak Up? How Group Network Density and Status Conflict Affect Group Voice
content: Although group network characteristics significantly influence a group’s capability to exchange and absorb knowledge by speaking up group members’ opinions, previous research on voice behavior has not yet fully addressed the social and relational factors in work groups that affect group-level voice. Specifically, in line with the “dark side of social capital” argument, this study examines the effects of group network density on group voice. In addition, drawing on the notion of status conflict, we further examine the moderating role of status conflict on relationships between group network density and group voice. Using data from 55 work groups, we found an inverted U-shaped relationship between group network density and group voice. Moreover, we found that the status conflict moderated the inverted-U effect of group density on group voice, such that: when status conflict is high, 1) overall, the level of group voice was reduced, 2) group voice turned to decrease faster on the downward side of the inverted-U curve. We discussed the theoretical and practical implications of these results with relation to effective group management.
